To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the usual dietary fatty acid intake of Inuit children aged from 11 to 53 months was low in n-3 and adequate in n-6 PUFAs and that the RBC membrane n-3 PUFAs of these children were positively associated with the consumption of breast-feeding and traditional food.
Inuit pre‐school children have poor n‐3 and n‐6 PUFA dietary intake and that this is reflected in their RBC membrane composition.
Inuit children aged between 11 months and 5 years in Nunavik are not consuming enough long-chain n-3 PUFAs, which are known to be beneficial to health.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between dietary fatty acid intake and RBC fatty acid composition among Inuit children.
the nutritional status of Inuit children and their parents.
the relationship between the intake of dietary fatty acids and their incorporation into the red blood cell membrane in a population with a high intake of n-3 fatty acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Inuit children in the present study are not getting enough n-3 fatty acid intake to maintain optimal health.

the present study provides further support to the hypothesis that dietary sources of n3 and n6 PUFAs are related to RBC n3 and n-PUFAs, and to the fact that the dietary sources of n6 PUFs are related to the RBC n6 PUFa levels.
the present study highlights that dietary intakes of n-3 PUFAs are not sufficient to achieve adequate n-3 PUFTA levels in the RBC membranes of Inuit children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present findings highlight the need to increase traditional food intakes among Inuit children.
Inuit children in Nunavik have inadequate intakes of n-3 PUFAs and n-6 PUFAs, and that these inadequacies are associated with RBC membrane n-3 PUFTA and n-6 fatty acid concentrations.
we need to improve the quality of the foods we eat and the quantity of foods we consume to improve our health.

Inuit children have a high proportion of inadequate n-3 PU FA intake.
